name: Lazarus MedCore Surgical Scrub — Augmented Cut
description: Lazarus's augmented-cut scrub set was developed in response to documented rates of augmentation-related surgical contamination — chrome port covers left open, cable routing creating sterile-field breaks, poorly designed garments forcing surgeons to improvise. The top features mapped port-access panels along the forearms and upper back, each sealed with a sterile-grade silicone flap that holds closed under normal movement but peels back under deliberate pressure. The fabric is a tri-layer antimicrobial weave that sheds biological contamination under standard autoclave cycling and repels fluid splash at the outer face. The color is Lazarus standard — a muted teal with white piping — and the Lazarus caduceus-cross logo sits at the upper left chest in bonded reflective film. Tail accommodation is handled through a structured rear vent in the trousers, reinforced so the seam doesn't fail during extended standing procedures.
cultural_context: In Lazarus facilities, the augmented-cut scrub is standard issue for any surgical staff with documented chrome. Wearing it in a non-Lazarus clinic signals either a Lazarus-trained surgeon or someone who lifted the set. The design has been widely copied by independent med-clinics in Tier 2 who can't afford Lazarus licensing but need the functionality.
story_hooks: A surgeon performing off-book procedures in a Tier 1 basement clinic wears a genuine augmented-cut set, raising questions about how they're sourcing Lazarus-restricted equipment.

The sterile-grade silicone port flaps on a recent production batch were manufactured with a microscopic RFID thread — Lazarus claims it's inventory management, but the tracking radius is far wider than any warehouse needs.
A Lazarus-employed surgeon's scrubs are found at the scene of a non-medical incident, still sealed in their sterile packaging, never worn.

physical_description.visual_profile: Clinical and purposeful — a surgical scrub cut with deliberate geometric precision. The silhouette reads medical-grade but augment-aware: forearms and upper back feature visible sealed panels that break the clean lines of traditional scrubs. The teal base reads institutional and calming; the white piping frames those functional access points like they're features, not compromises. On a person with visible chrome, the garment reads as intentional accommodation rather than afterthought.
physical_description.fit: Tailored but not restrictive — designed to allow full range of motion during long surgical procedures without pulling or snagging on integrated augmentation. The top sits close through the torso to prevent fabric drift across sterile fields, while the trousers feature a structured rear vent that won't gape or bunch during extended standing. Cuffs are fitted but not compression-tight, allowing easy access to forearm port covers.
physical_description.primary_material: Tri-layer antimicrobial weave — outer face ballistic-grade synthetic for fluid repellency, middle layer of treated bio-resistant composite, inner face soft brushed polymer that won't irritate skin or augmentation junction points. Designed to survive autoclave cycling without degradation.
physical_description.texture: Smooth outer face with subtle micro-texture to prevent fluid beading, matte finish rather than reflective. The sealed silicone flaps over port access panels have a slightly tacky, medical-grade feel. Seams are sealed with bonded thread and feel rigid compared to standard surgical scrubs. Overall impression: precision-engineered rather than soft.
physical_description.color_scheme: Lazarus institutional teal (a muted, desaturated cyan) as primary. Crisp white piping frames all port-access panels and runs along seams and cuffs. The Lazarus caduceus-cross logo in the upper left chest rendered in bonded reflective film that catches light at oblique angles. No patterns — the visual interest comes from the panel geometry and piping layout.
physical_description.closures: Top closes with a center zip that runs from chest to lower abdomen, with a pull-tab sized for gloved operation. Trousers feature an elastic waistband with internal drawstring for secure, one-handed adjustment. All port-access panels are sealed with pressure-sensitive medical-grade silicone flaps that hold closed under normal movement and peel back only under deliberate pressure — a design feature that prevents accidental exposure.
distinctive_features: Mapped port-access panels along both forearms and upper back, each sealed with sterile-grade silicone flaps
White piping that frames each access panel, creating visual hierarchy and functional landmarks
Tri-layer antimicrobial weave construction designed to shed biological contamination under autoclave cycling
Structured rear vent in trousers reinforced to prevent seam failure during extended standing procedures
Lazarus caduceus-cross logo in bonded reflective film at upper left chest
Sealed seams throughout using bonded thread rather than standard stitching
Fluid-repellent outer face that prevents splash penetration
Cuffs fitted but accessible for easy forearm port cover inspection
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 3-4 functional professional wear — too specialized and expensive for Tier 5, too utilitarian for Tier 1-2 corpo fashion. The reflective logo and precision engineering signal institutional backing and training, not luxury.
physical_description.cultural_context: Within Lazarus Medical Systems facilities, wearing the augmented-cut scrub is standard issue for any surgical staff with documented chrome augmentation. In the broader GLMZ, it signals either legitimate Lazarus training or black-market acquisition. Independent med-clinics in Tier 2 have spawned knockoffs because the design solves genuine augmentation-accommodation problems that standard scrubs ignore. Wearing it outside a medical context reads as either stolen or identity-confused.
physical_description.condition_typical: When properly maintained: pristine, with the teal rich and the white piping still bright. The silicone flaps show the most wear first — slight discoloration from repeated peeling and oil buildup. After extended use: micro-staining from blood and biological spray despite the antimicrobial treatment, minor creasing at articulation points, the bonded logo showing faint scratches from gloved contact. Old Lazarus scrubs in the field often have hand-sewn reinforcements around the rear vent seam or improvised patches where the designed access flaps didn't hold up under real surgical stress.
